name: American Express
summary: American Express interviews usually combine behavioural questions on its Blue Box Values, such as 'We Back Our Customers' and 'We Do What's Right', with technical or case questions for the role, from software engineering to analytics, risk and marketing. Candidates commonly report a recruiter screen, interviews with the hiring manager, and a final round with the wider team.
rounds: Online application, with an online assessment or coding test for some roles
Interviews with the hiring manager: your experience, behavioural questions and technical or case questions
Final round with the wider team; for some student programmes, an assessment centre with case studies
looks_for: We Stand for Equity and Inclusion
Careful use of data and sound judgement on risk
Clear communication with colleagues, customers and partners

questions.text: Tell me about yourself and why you're interested in this role.
covers: Your background in a few lines, focused on what's relevant
One achievement that shows the skills the role needs
Why this team at American Express is the next step

questions.text: Tell me about a time you went out of your way to fix a problem for a customer or user.
covers: Who they were and what was going wrong for them
What you did beyond the usual, and why
The result for them, and anything you changed so it didn't recur

questions.text: Tell me about a time you raised the quality bar on a piece of work.
covers: What 'good enough' looked like and why you aimed higher
What you improved and how you checked it
The difference it made, ideally measured

questions.text: Tell me about a time you chose the right course of action over the quickest one.
covers: The shortcut and why it was tempting
Why you didn't take it, and who you involved
The outcome and what it taught you

questions.text: Describe a time your team succeeded because of how you worked together, not only individual effort.
covers: The goal and who was on the team
How you shared work, helped each other and handled disagreement
The result and your part in it

questions.text: How would you decide whether to approve a credit limit increase for a cardholder? What data would you use?
covers: Repayment history, current balances, income signals and how the card is used
Weighing extra spending and customer loyalty against the risk of default
How you'd test the rule fairly and monitor it once live

questions.text: A new card's sign-ups are strong, but spending per card is lower than expected. How would you investigate?
covers: Checking whether new cardholders are activating the card and using it at all
Splitting by customer group, channel and merchant type
Likely causes and what you'd test: offers, reminders, or a change in who's being targeted

questions.text: Explain how a card payment works from the moment a customer pays to when the merchant gets the money.
covers: The parties: cardholder, merchant, card network and card issuer
Authorisation at the time of payment, then clearing and settlement
Where fees are charged and where fraud checks happen

questions.text: How would you design a service that flags possibly fraudulent card transactions within a second?
covers: A fast scoring step using rules and a model, with features such as location and spending pattern
What happens next: approve, decline or ask the customer to confirm
Keeping it fast and available, learning from confirmed fraud, and protecting customer data

questions.text: Explain precision and recall to a business partner, and which matters more in fraud detection.
covers: Precision: of the cases flagged, how many were really fraud; recall: of all fraud, how much was caught
The trade-off: catching more fraud versus annoying good customers
How you'd choose the balance using the cost of each kind of mistake

questions.text: Walk me through a project where you used data to change a decision.
covers: The decision and who was making it
The data and methods you used
What changed because of your work

questions.text: Why American Express, and why this team?
covers: Something specific about how American Express serves its customers
What the team does and why it fits your skills
What you'd want to learn in your first year

questions.text: Which Blue Box Value means the most to you, and when have you shown it?
covers: One value, named once
A short, specific example
Why it matters in the role you've applied for

tips: Prepare a story for each Blue Box Value, especially backing customers and doing what's right.
For analytics and risk roles, be ready to talk through how you'd measure a customer decision and what could go wrong with it.
For engineering roles, expect coding plus a design discussion; bring up security, reliability and protection of customer data.
Learn how card payments work end to end, and what makes a card valuable to both cardholders and merchants.
Ask the recruiter what each interview will focus on, so you can prepare the right mix of stories and technical work.
